newsitem.title: FRANCE: Netanyahu appeals to Mubarak on Jerusalem violence.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu appeals to Mubarak on Jerusalem violence.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu appealed to Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Wednesday to help calm Arab violence sparked by Israel's opening of a tunnel under the Old City of Jerusalem.
Netanyahu told reporters he telephoned Mubarak from French Prime Minister Alain Juppe's office during a visit to Paris.
"I asked him to use his influence in the Arab world and with the Palestinians to urge them to return to the table, to cease violence and to negotiate," he said.

"I thought it was important for any leader in the Middle East that is in a position to do so to calm the atmosphere...I said to President Mubarak that it is my sincere belief that peace and tranquillity is in the interest of both Palestinians and Israelis," he said.
"I am hopeful this will be achieved in the coming days."
Netanyahu was speaking after Israeli troops shot dead three Palestinian protesters and wounded up to 300 near the West Bank town of Ramallah, according to Arab hospital officials.
It was the worst violence since Netanyahu's hardline government, opposed to trading occupied Arab land for peace, took office 100 days ago.

The Israeli premier urged Arab leaders to exercise restraint and be careful with the facts over the disputed tunnel, which he insisted did not run under Temple Mount, site of Islam's third holiest shrine.
Asked if he would also call Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, Netanyahu said: "If there is a need, I will also speak (with Arafat)."
A senior Israeli official travelling with Netanyahu charged that Arafat was behind Wednesday's violence and that Palestinian police had been told not to intervene to prevent violence.

"In Ramallah, there was a deliberate attempt to push the demonstrators towards Israeli soldiers. Apparently, guidelines were given to Palestinian police not to intervene. It looks like a well-organised attempt to apply pressure on us," the official told reporters.
Asked whether he would cut short his trip to Britain, France and Germany, Netanyahu said he only that he was in constant contact with Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai.
